senses.definition: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.

quotes.text: She was like a Beardsley Salome, he had said. And indeed she had the narrow eyes and the high cheekbone of that creature, and as nearly the sinuosity as is compatible with human symmetry.

senses.definition: Of little extent; very limited; circumscribed.

quotes.text: The Jews were but a small nation, and confined to a narrow compass in the world.

senses.definition: Having a small margin or degree.
examples: The Republicans won by a narrow majority.

quotes.text: Although we lost the election by the narrowest of margins, the people of Oregon heard a great deal about education, and particularly about how "look-say" reading instruction was hardshipping Oregon school children.

senses.definition: Scrutinizing in detail; close; accurate; exact.

quotes.text: But first with narrow search I must walk round / This garden, and no corner leave unspied.

senses.definition: (phonetics) Formed (as a vowel) by a close position of some part of the tongue in relation to the palate; or (according to Bell) by a tense condition of the pharynx; distinguished from wide.
(computing) Of or supporting only those text characters that can fit into the traditional 8-bit representation.
examples: a narrow character; a narrow stream

senses.definition: (chiefly in the plural) A narrow passage, especially a contracted part of a stream, lake, or sea; a strait connecting two bodies of water.
examples: the narrows of New York harbor

quotes.text: Near the island lay on one side the jaws of a dangerous narrow.
quotes.reference: 1858, William Gladstone, Studies on Homer and the Homeric Age:

senses.definition: (transitive) To reduce in width or extent; to contract.
examples: We need to narrow the search.

senses.definition: (of a person or eyes) To partially lower one's eyelids in a way usually taken to suggest a defensive, aggressive or penetrating look.
examples: He stepped in front of me, narrowing his eyes to slits.
She wagged her finger in his face, and her eyes narrowed.

senses.definition: (knitting) To contract the size of, as a stocking, by taking two stitches into one.
(transitive, programming) To convert to a data type that cannot hold as many distinct values.
examples: to narrow an int variable to a short variable
